schoen1970.entry: Schoen, A. H. (1970). Infinite periodic minimal surfaces without self-intersections. NASA Technical Note TN D-5541. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19700020472
schoen1970.scope: Introduced the gyroid. Cite for the gyroid's origin only, not for its trigonometric approximation.

vonschnering1991.entry: von Schnering, H. G., & Nesper, R. (1991). Nodal surfaces of Fourier series: Fundamental invariants of structured matter. Zeitschrift für Physik B Condensed Matter, 83(3), 407-412. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01313411
vonschnering1991.scope: Periodic nodal surfaces of short Fourier series; cite for using nodal (level-set) approximations such as sin x cos y + ... for TPMS families.

alketan2021.entry: Al-Ketan, O., & Abu Al-Rub, R. K. (2021). MSLattice: A free software for generating uniform and graded lattices based on triply periodic minimal surfaces. Material Design & Processing Communications, 3(6), e205. https://doi.org/10.1002/mdp2.205
alketan2021.scope: Sheet versus solid (skeletal) TPMS networks, level-set offset or sheet thickness controlling relative density, uniform and graded density, cell-size grading, hybrid lattices.

parlayan2023.entry: Parlayan, O. A., Ozdemir, M., Gayir, C. E., Simsek, U., & Kiziltas, G. (2023). A new sensitivity-based mapping scheme for topology optimization of graded TPMS designs. The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology, 129(7-8), 3197-3220. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-023-12439-1
parlayan2023.scope: Mapping a topology-optimisation result onto locally graded gyroids using sensitivities rather than relative density. Cite as the origin of optimisation-driven grading; corpus examples only use proxy fields, not this method.

sigmund1994.entry: Sigmund, O. (1994). Materials with prescribed constitutive parameters: An inverse homogenization problem. International Journal of Solids and Structures, 31(17), 2313-2329. https://doi.org/10.1016/0020-7683(94)90154-6
sigmund1994.scope: Inverse homogenisation: designing periodic microstructures for prescribed effective properties. Not a TPMS paper; cite only for the homogenisation idea behind cell-level property design.

cloots2013.entry: Cloots, M., Spierings, A. B., & Wegener, K. (2013). Assessing new support minimizing strategies for the additive manufacturing technology SLM. Proceedings of the 24th International Solid Freeform Fabrication Symposium, Austin, TX, 631-643. https://utw10945.utweb.utexas.edu/Manuscripts/2013/2013-50-Cloots.pdf
cloots2013.scope: 316L on a Concept Laser M2: unsupported overhangs of 30 deg built with all 16 parameter sets, 25 deg only with poor quality in some cases, 20 deg only with a 0 deg scan angle. The paper cites 45 deg from earlier work as the angle below which surface quality may degrade; it does NOT establish 45 deg as a hard limit.

cloots2017.entry: Cloots, M., Zumofen, L., Spierings, A. B., Kirchheim, A., & Wegener, K. (2017). Approaches to minimize overhang angles of SLM parts. Rapid Prototyping Journal, 23(2), 362-369. https://doi.org/10.1108/RPJ-05-2015-0061
cloots2017.scope: Support-free surfaces at or below 30 deg on two commercial machines with a shell-core approach and contour-like exposure; process-specific.

kokkonen2016.entry: Kokkonen, P., Salonen, L., Virta, J., Hemming, B., Laukkanen, P., Savolainen, M., Komi, E., Junttila, J., Ruusuvuori, K., Varjus, S., Vaajoki, A., Kivi, S., & Welling, J. (2016). Design guide for additive manufacturing of metal components by SLM process. VTT Research Report VTT-R-03160-16. VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland. https://sarjaweb.vtt.fi/julkaisut/muut/2016/VTT-R-03160-16.pdf
kokkonen2016.scope: Downward surfaces at less than 45 deg to the platform need supports (section 2.6); unsupported horizontal overhangs beyond one to two millimetres are not recommended (3.10.4); small-diameter holes are better drilled after printing (Fig. 81); fillets help overhangs. Test materials 316L, H13, Inconel, AlSi12.

mercelis2006.entry: Mercelis, P., & Kruth, J.-P. (2006). Residual stresses in selective laser sintering and selective laser melting. Rapid Prototyping Journal, 12(5), 254-265. https://doi.org/10.1108/13552540610707013
mercelis2006.scope: Residual stress profile with large tensile zones at the top and bottom of the part and compression between; main factors are material properties, sample and substrate height, scan strategy and heating conditions. Experiments in 316L only.

kranz2015.entry: Kranz, J., Herzog, D., & Emmelmann, C. (2015). Design guidelines for laser additive manufacturing of lightweight structures in TiAl6V4. Journal of Laser Applications, 27(S1), S14001. https://doi.org/10.2351/1.4885235
kranz2015.scope: Build orientation and position affect dimensional accuracy and surface quality of thin walls, bars and bores in TiAl6V4. Do not quote numeric minimum wall or hole sizes from it (not read).

lamarche2024.entry: Lamarche-Gagnon, M.-É., Molavi-Zarandi, M., Raymond, V., & Ilinca, F. (2024). Additively manufactured conformal cooling channels through topology optimization. Structural and Multidisciplinary Optimization, 67(8), 138. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-024-03846-3
lamarche2024.scope: Uses 45 deg from the build plate, build direction (0,0,1), as the overhang threshold in a topology-optimisation overhang constraint for conformal cooling channels. Cite for 45 deg as a common conservative design default.

curless1996.entry: Curless, B., & Levoy, M. (1996). A volumetric method for building complex models from range images. Proceedings of SIGGRAPH 96, 303-312. https://doi.org/10.1145/237170.237269
curless1996.scope: Cumulative weighted signed distance on a voxel grid, fusing range images with D = (W D + w d)/(W + w). Assumes range images with known sensor line of sight, not unordered point clouds.

hoppe1992.entry: Hoppe, H., DeRose, T., Duchamp, T., McDonald, J., & Stuetzle, W. (1992). Surface reconstruction from unorganized points. ACM SIGGRAPH Computer Graphics, 26(2), 71-78. https://doi.org/10.1145/142920.134011
hoppe1992.scope: Signed distance to tangent planes estimated from k nearest neighbours of unorganised points, with consistent normal orientation; the right citation for unordered .xyz/.csv clouds without sensor poses.

museth2013.entry: Museth, K. (2013). VDB: High-resolution sparse volumes with dynamic topology. ACM Transactions on Graphics, 32(3), 27:1-27:22. https://doi.org/10.1145/2487228.2487235
museth2013.scope: The sparse narrow-band level-set data structure (OpenVDB) underlying PicoGK voxels.

serra1982.entry: Serra, J. (1982). Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology. Academic Press, London.
serra1982.scope: Erosion, dilation, opening and closing; cite for morphological opening/closing implemented with PicoGK offsets.

ramos2025.entry: Ramos, A., Angel, V. G., Siqueiros, M., Sahagun, T., Gonzalez, L., & Ballesteros, R. (2025). Reviewing additive manufacturing techniques: Material trends and weight optimization possibilities through innovative printing patterns. Materials, 18(6), 1377. https://doi.org/10.3390/ma18061377 (CC BY 4.0)
ramos2025.scope: Review, qualitative only: LPBF metal parts need supports against warping and distortion; SLM support removal is critical because high thermal gradients cause significant residual stress; stress-relief annealing and HIP (porosity, fatigue) are common post-processes; SLM roughness often needs machining or electrochemical polishing; AlSi10Mg and AlSi12 are the most used aluminium AM alloys. Its gyroid/infill section is about FDM slicer infill; never cite it for metal process parameters or LPBF lattice mechanics.

dubey2024.entry: Dubey, D., Singh, S. P., & Behera, B. K. (2024). A review on recent advancements in additive manufacturing techniques. Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part E: Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering, 240(3), 3534-3556. https://doi.org/10.1177/09544089241275860
dubey2024.scope: Review, abstract only read: classifies AM into the seven ASTM process categories, including powder bed fusion. Cite only for that taxonomy.

iso52911.entry: ISO/ASTM 52911-1:2019. Additive manufacturing - Design - Part 1: Laser-based powder bed fusion of metals. ISO, Geneva.
iso52911.scope: Standard giving design recommendations for PBF-LB/M. Content not read here: cite only as the applicable design standard, never for specific numbers.

wade2025.entry: Wade, C., Beck, D., & MacCurdy, R. (2025). Implicit modeling for 3D-printed multi-material computational object design via Python. Proceedings of the ACM Symposium on Computational Fabrication (SCF '25), 1-16. https://doi.org/10.1145/3745778.3766659 (preprint arXiv:2509.15562)
wade2025.scope: Implicit/SDF modelling with volume-fraction functions; programmatic lattice grading at global, per-cell and per-strut level; describes PicoGK as an OpenVDB-based engineering voxel workflow without multi-material support. Prints were polymer only: do not cite for metal LPBF manufacturability or properties.

borisov2025.entry: Borisov, E. V., Repnin, A. V., & Popovich, A. A. (2025). Additive manufacturing of functionally graded products by selective laser melting: A review. Powder Metallurgy and Functional Coatings, 19(4), 77-90. https://doi.org/10.17073/1997-308X-2025-4-77-90 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
borisov2025.scope: Review of multi-material / functionally graded SLM: interface zone widths (about 300 um at 50 um layers for VZh159/BrKhZrTV, overlap zone about 350-400 um), pre-deformed models to compensate warping (no numbers). Never cite it for what PicoGK is (its description is wrong).

barill2018.entry: Barill, G., Dickson, N. G., Schmidt, R., Levin, D. I. W., & Jacobson, A. (2018). Fast winding numbers for soups and clouds. ACM Transactions on Graphics, 37(4), 1-12. https://doi.org/10.1145/3197517.3201337
barill2018.scope: Generalised winding number for triangle soups and oriented point clouds: each point contributes its area times its normal as a dipole, giving about 1 inside and 0 outside, robust to holes, noise and non-manifold input. Cite for the winding-number inside test. Corpus code lumps far samples per grid cell; it does not implement the paper's tree and Taylor expansions.

tang2017.entry: Tang, M., Pistorius, P. C., & Beuth, J. L. (2017). Prediction of lack-of-fusion porosity for powder bed fusion. Additive Manufacturing, 14, 39-48. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.addma.2016.12.001
tang2017.scope: Geometric lack-of-fusion criterion from melt-pool width and depth, hatch spacing and layer thickness: (h/W)^2 + (L/D)^2 <= 1 for full overlap. Cite for that criterion only; it predicts the onset of lack-of-fusion porosity, not part quality or other defect types.

coleman2025.entry: Coleman, J., Kincaid, K., Knapp, G. L., Stump, B., Reeve, S. T., Rolchigo, M., & Plotkowski, A. (2025). AdditiveFOAM: A continuum multiphysics code for additive manufacturing. Journal of Open Source Software, 10(109), 7770. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07770
coleman2025.scope: The open-source OpenFOAM-based heat and mass transfer solver for melt-pool simulation used for this project's process evidence. Cite as the software; it does not calibrate a machine or qualify parts.

knapp2023.entry: Knapp, G. L., Coleman, J., Rolchigo, M., Stoyanov, M., & Plotkowski, A. (2023). Calibrating uncertain parameters in melt pool simulations of additive manufacturing. Computational Materials Science, 218, 111904. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.commatsci.2022.111904
knapp2023.scope: Calibration of melt-pool simulation parameters against AM-Bench 2018 IN625 single tracks; the origin of AdditiveFOAM's calibrated single-track tutorial. Cite for that calibration only.

lane2020.entry: Lane, B., Heigel, J., Ricker, R., Zhirnov, I., Khromschenko, V., Weaver, J., Phan, T., Stoudt, M., Mekhontsev, S., & Levine, L. (2020). Measurements of melt pool geometry and cooling rates of individual laser traces on IN625 bare plates. Integrating Materials and Manufacturing Innovation, 9(1), 16-30. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40192-020-00169-1
lane2020.scope: AM-Bench 2018 (AMB2018-02) measurements of melt-pool width, depth and cooling rate for single laser traces on IN625 bare plates. Cite for those reference measurements only.

barequet1995.entry: Barequet, G., & Sharir, M. (1995). Filling gaps in the boundary of a polyhedron. Computer Aided Geometric Design, 12(2), 207-229. https://doi.org/10.1016/0167-8396(94)00011-G
barequet1995.scope: Repairing polyhedral boundaries with gaps: boundary loops are identified and each remaining hole is closed by a minimum-area triangulation found by an O(n^3) dynamic program over the loop's vertex order. Cite for the hole-triangulation step. Corpus code fills each boundary loop independently; it does not implement the paper's matching of boundary chains across gaps.

gumruk2013.entry: Gümrük, R., & Mines, R. A. W. (2013). Compressive behaviour of stainless steel micro-lattice structures. International Journal of Mechanical Sciences, 68, 125-139. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijmecsci.2013.01.006
gumruk2013.scope: Static compression of 316L body-centred cubic (BCC) micro-lattices made by selective laser melting, with Timoshenko beam models for the initial stiffness that account for material overlap at the strut joints; the response is governed by the strut aspect ratio. Abstract-level only (full text not read): cite for BCC strut lattices being built by SLM and modelled as beams, never for numbers or for BCC-Z results.

deshpande2001.entry: Deshpande, V. S., Ashby, M. F., & Fleck, N. A. (2001). Foam topology: bending versus stretching dominated architectures. Acta Materialia, 49(6), 1035-1040. https://doi.org/10.1016/S1359-6454(00)00379-7
deshpande2001.scope: Classifies cellular architectures as bending- or stretching-dominated from their nodal connectivity, a Maxwell-type rigidity argument; stretching-dominated lattices are stiffer and stronger at the same relative density. Full text not read here: cite only for the qualitative classification, never for numbers or connectivity thresholds.
